The World-Tree Stands Tall

Act I · Layout

The tree grows upward

the decree

We need a tree with more verticality and less width. Make the lanterns all fit within a tree moving up vertically with half the width of this tree

The decree: the world-tree must climb, not sprawl. The lanterns were reseated as a zigzag ladder up a drawn trunk — seats spanning a third of the panel's width but double its height — while every vine learned to curl out to a fixed branch rail at 44% and descend it, so job cards hang in the open sky and never crowd the trunk.

The wide painting could not host so narrow a tree, so it was set aside (preserved as backdrop.jpg) and a tapering SVG trunk drawn in its place — bark, moss sheen, root flare, stars. Measured in a live browser: lanterns clear the card rail by fifteen pixels standard, three compact.

Act II · Design

The painted tree returns

the decree

It's not a tree anymore! generate a tree image to use keep all the same styles ensure the prompt to generate the tree with /imagen is committed — and find the initial prompt that was used

The drawn trunk was too abstract — it was not a tree anymore. The original prompt was recovered where it had always been inscribed, in src/ui/assets/README.md: a moonlit tree of life, moss-covered trunk, deep blue-greens, painterly, no text. Twelve variants were painted over three rolls before one stood worthy: a tall narrow tree in the left third, eleven pale leaf-lanterns climbing its full height, cool moonlit palette, no swirls.

Seats were vision-mapped onto the painted lanterns and stored in painting %, with a projection that follows the painting through any panel width. The tall prompt was committed beside the wide one, so the tree can always be regrown.

function projectSeat(p) {
  if (state.mode === "compact") return { x: p.x, y: p.y };  // fill: painting == scene
  const k = Math.max(W / 896, H / 1200);                    // cover-center
  const dw = 896 * k, fl = -(dw - W) / 2;
  return { x: (p.x / 100 * dw + fl) / W * 100, y: p.y };
}

Act III · Tooling

imagen joins the pack

the decree

move the imagen skill into the pack and reconfigure to use it — make sure it's removed from fenrir

The /imagen generator — the brush that painted every profile icon and now the tree itself — left its birthplace in fenrir-ledger and became pack property: claude-pack/skills/imagen, frontmatter rewritten to the pack convention, the 1Password key retrieval and the JPEG-under-a-.png-name trap inscribed in its SKILL.md.

fenrir-ledger's own copy was struck from main — a real directory deleted, replaced by the standard ../pack/skills/imagen symlink and a submodule bump. Hermes received it at ~/.hermes/skills/pack/imagen, and the ai-image-generation skill was repointed. Every repo in the fleet can now paint.

Act IV · UI

Stones claim the lanterns

the decree

the stones must overlay the lanterns and ensure the lanterns are dimmed if that namespace is not active. There are 11 lanterns so that accommodates a max of 11 active namespaces. Ensure the scrolling task list always attaches to its lantern

Each namespace now seats as a stone — a dark slate disc laid over its painted lantern, carrying the world's icon. The pool became the eleven painted lanterns exactly: one seat per lantern, a max of eleven active namespaces, and the API answers a twelfth world with the tree is full — eleven lanterns shine.

The older flaw was subtler: the painting and its stones stood still while the vine scrolled, and the strand tore away from its lantern. The whole scene — painting, stones, vine, cards — was gathered into one scrolling canvas, pinned to the scene's height and growing below into night. Now the task list can never leave its stone.

The Mend

The vine detached from its lantern on scroll: lanterns lived in a static overlay while the vine scrolled in a separate layer, so any scroll tore the strand from its origin. Fixed structurally — one canvas, one scroll, everything attached.

Act V · Refinement

Only one stone wakes

the decree

The dimmed ones are more obvious than the active ones, they should fade to the background and in the Z index too — and ensure there are all aligned up and multiple namespaces have tasks

A quiet stone of dark slate against a glowing painted lantern shouted louder than the waking one. The sleeping stones were taught to fade: ghost-transparent, no rim, no shadow, the painted glow shining through them, dropped below the active stone in z-order. Hover coaxes a stone half-awake; only the chosen world's stone opens — translucent, teal-ringed, unmistakable.

Every world's summary now arrives at boot, so six namespaces show their berries and task rows at once — the tree reads as a living ledger, not a lone open vine.

The Mend

Visual hierarchy inverted: opaque dimmed stones outweighed the single active stone. Fixed with ghost opacity, transparent rim, scale, and z-index 4 beneath the active stone's 7.

Act VI · Delivery

The decree: make it so

the decree

yes looks good make it so

Approval spoken, the machinery turned. Issue #69 was filed carrying the whole v3.9 contract — the prototype its scripture — and FiremanDecko was fired to GKE: 104 turns, $4.91, a decree of PASS on every check — tsc clean, ten suites of ten, build green.

PR #70 came back mergeable-clean and was squash-merged: nine files, the tall painting swapped in byte for byte, projectSeat and the eleven seats in treeSeats.ts, the stone skin mirrored into the desktop plugin in the same breath. The desktop mirror was rebuilt from fresh main, the Deploy-to-GKE workflow ran, and the hall answered healthz: 200. The vertical world-tree stands on every surface.
